lines.text: One hundred fractions with square roots, all added up. Sounds like a calculator job, right?
lines.caption: One hundred fractions with square roots, all added up. Sounds like a calculator job, right?

lines.text: Here's the surprise. You can pin it down with NO calculator at all.
lines.caption: Here's the surprise. You can pin it down with NO calculator at all.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's trap this sum between a floor and a ceiling.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's trap this sum between a floor and a ceiling.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Add one over root one, plus one over root two, and so on, up to one over root one hundred.
lines.caption: Add one over root one, plus one over root two, and so on, up to one over root one hundred.

lines.text: What is the greatest whole number less than or equal to this sum?
lines.caption: What is the greatest whole number less than or equal to this sum?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what are we really looking for? Not the exact sum. Just the sum, rounded down.
lines.caption: So what are we really looking for? Not the exact sum. Just the sum, rounded down.

lines.text: If the sum sits between two whole numbers next to each other, the smaller one is our answer.
lines.caption: If the sum sits between two whole numbers next to each other, the smaller one is our answer.

lines.text: Every term is at least one over ten, and at most one. So the sum is between ten and one hundred.
lines.caption: Every term is at least one over ten, and at most one. So the sum is between ten and one hundred.

lines.text: That window is way too wide. We need a sharper floor and ceiling.
lines.caption: That window is way too wide. We need a sharper floor and ceiling.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's our plan: turn each term into a picture.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's our plan: turn each term into a picture.

lines.text: Draw a square with area k. Its side is root k.
lines.caption: Draw a square with area k. Its side is root k.

lines.text: Now grow it to area k plus one. Its side becomes root of k plus one.
lines.caption: Now grow it to area k plus one. Its side becomes root of k plus one.

lines.text: The new part is an L-shaped strip, with area exactly one. Call its thickness g, the gap.
lines.caption: The new part is an L-shaped strip, with area exactly one. Call its thickness g, the gap.

lines.text: Cut the strip into two rectangles, both g thick. One is root k long, the other is a bit longer.
lines.caption: Cut the strip into two rectangles, both g thick. One is root k long, the other is a bit longer.

lines.text: So the strip's area, one, is MORE than g times two root k.
lines.caption: So the strip's area, one, is MORE than g times two root k.

lines.text: Divide both sides by root k. Two g is less than one over root k. Each term beats two gaps!
lines.caption: Divide both sides by root k. Two g is less than one over root k. Each term beats two gaps!

lines.text: Now do this for every k, from one to one hundred. The squares nest inside each other.
lines.caption: Now do this for every k, from one to one hundred. The squares nest inside each other.

lines.text: All the gaps together grow the side from one to root one hundred one.
lines.caption: All the gaps together grow the side from one to root one hundred one.

lines.text: So the sum is more than two times, root one hundred one minus one.
lines.caption: So the sum is more than two times, root one hundred one minus one.

lines.text: Root one hundred one is a bit more than ten, because ten squared is one hundred.
lines.caption: Root one hundred one is a bit more than ten, because ten squared is one hundred.

lines.text: So the sum is more than two times nine. That's eighteen! There's our floor.
lines.caption: So the sum is more than two times nine. That's eighteen! There's our floor.

lines.text: Next, a ceiling. This time, use the strip just INSIDE the square with side root k.
lines.caption: Next, a ceiling. This time, use the strip just INSIDE the square with side root k.

lines.text: Grow a square from area k minus one to area k. Again, the strip has area one.
lines.caption: Grow a square from area k minus one to area k. Again, the strip has area one.

lines.text: Call its thickness h. Now both rectangles are at most root k long.
lines.caption: Call its thickness h. Now both rectangles are at most root k long.

lines.text: So one is LESS than h times two root k. Each term is less than two of these gaps.
lines.caption: So one is LESS than h times two root k. Each term is less than two of these gaps.

lines.text: Careful with the very first term! When k is one, that only says one is less than two.
lines.caption: Careful with the very first term! When k is one, that only says one is less than two.

lines.text: So keep the first term as exactly one, and squeeze the other ninety-nine.
lines.caption: So keep the first term as exactly one, and squeeze the other ninety-nine.

lines.text: Their gaps grow the side from root one to root one hundred. That's from one to ten.
lines.caption: Their gaps grow the side from root one to root one hundred. That's from one to ten.

lines.text: So the sum is less than one, plus two times nine. That's nineteen!
lines.caption: So the sum is less than one, plus two times nine. That's nineteen!

lines.text: The sum is more than eighteen, and less than nineteen.
lines.caption: The sum is more than eighteen, and less than nineteen.

lines.text: Round it down, and the answer is <short pause> eighteen! Choice C.
lines.caption: Round it down, and the answer is eighteen! Choice C.

lines.text: A computer agrees. The sum is a bit more than eighteen and a half.
lines.caption: A computer agrees. The sum is a bit more than eighteen and a half.

lines.text: Here's a faster way to get the lower bound, with algebra.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way to get the lower bound, with algebra.

lines.text: Multiply root of k plus one, minus root k, by the same two roots added.
lines.caption: Multiply root of k plus one, minus root k, by the same two roots added.

lines.text: Difference of squares! You get k plus one, minus k. That's just one.
lines.caption: Difference of squares! You get k plus one, minus k. That's just one.

lines.text: So the gap equals one over, root of k plus one, plus root k.
lines.caption: So the gap equals one over, root of k plus one, plus root k.

lines.text: That bottom is bigger than two root k. So two gaps are less than one over root k.
lines.caption: That bottom is bigger than two root k. So two gaps are less than one over root k.

lines.text: Add them up, and every middle square root cancels. Only the two ends stay.
lines.caption: Add them up, and every middle square root cancels. Only the two ends stay.

lines.text: When would you pick this one? On test day. It's just a few lines.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? On test day. It's just a few lines.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: A, ten, is what you'd get from every term being at least one over ten. True, but way too low.
lines.caption: A, ten, is what you'd get from every term being at least one over ten. True, but way too low.

lines.text: B, seventeen, is too small. Our floor already beat eighteen.
lines.caption: B, seventeen, is too small. Our floor already beat eighteen.

lines.text: D, nineteen, is what you'd get from the ceiling alone. But the sum stays UNDER nineteen.
lines.caption: D, nineteen, is what you'd get from the ceiling alone. But the sum stays UNDER nineteen.

lines.text: E, twenty, is what you'd get from two root one hundred, forgetting to subtract anything.
lines.caption: E, twenty, is what you'd get from two root one hundred, forgetting to subtract anything.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. One wall isn't enough. You need a floor AND a ceiling.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. One wall isn't enough. You need a floor AND a ceiling.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, but way more terms.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same idea, but way more terms.

lines.text: Add one over root one, all the way up to one over root ten thousand.
lines.caption: Add one over root one, all the way up to one over root ten thousand.

lines.text: What is the greatest whole number less than or equal to this sum?
lines.caption: What is the greatest whole number less than or equal to this sum?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: For the floor, the side grows from one to root ten thousand one, just over one hundred.
lines.caption: For the floor, the side grows from one to root ten thousand one, just over one hundred.

lines.text: So the sum is more than two times ninety-nine. That's one hundred ninety-eight.
lines.caption: So the sum is more than two times ninety-nine. That's one hundred ninety-eight.

lines.text: For the ceiling, keep the first term as one. The rest grow the side from one to one hundred.
lines.caption: For the ceiling, keep the first term as one. The rest grow the side from one to one hundred.

lines.text: So the sum is less than one, plus one hundred ninety-eight. That's one hundred ninety-nine.
lines.caption: So the sum is less than one, plus one hundred ninety-eight. That's one hundred ninety-nine.

lines.text: The answer is one hundred ninety-eight! Ten thousand terms, and no calculator.
lines.caption: The answer is one hundred ninety-eight! Ten thousand terms, and no calculator.

lines.text: The big idea: squeeze each term between two easy pieces. Add them up, and the middle cancels.
lines.caption: The big idea: squeeze each term between two easy pieces. Add them up, and the middle cancels.

lines.text: Then a floor and a ceiling, one apart, tell you the whole number.
lines.caption: Then a floor and a ceiling, one apart, tell you the whole number.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
